content.title: What is draft age limit? Army raises enlistment age, what to know
content.text: April 3, 2026, 1:40 p.m. ETThe U.S. Army recently raised the enlistment age limit for eligible recruits as the United States deploys more troops to the Middle East and the Iran war raises questions and concerns about a possible military draft among Americans.Here's what to know about draft and enlistment ages, Selective Service requirements, and who would be exempt.The Army announced a new age limit change from 35 to 42 years of age in a memo this week that also included removing a waiver requirement for recruits that have a single marijuana or drug paraphernalia conviction, according to reports.The new army enlistment age came amid President Donald Trump's claims that the United States is negotiating a 15-point peace plan with Iran, while reports of up to 3,000 US Army paratroopers from the 82nd Airborne Division are preparing to deploy to the Middle East.The number of American troops injured in the Iran war has climbed over 200 and 13 American service members have died thus far as the war rages on for the 26th day.While no draft has been called, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said the president is not ruling out American troops on the ground in Iran or a military draft, "President Donald Trump wisely doesn't remove options off of the table." Adding, "The president, as commander in chief, wants to continue to assess the success of this military operation. It's not part of the current plan right now, but the president, again, wisely wants to keep his options on the table."The last time a draft call was issued in the United States was in 1972 during the Vietnam War. There is no draft at present.Here's what to know about the Army's new enlistment age limit, the Selective Service System, and how the draft would work or who gets drafted first.What is the new enlistment age for the U.S. Army?Effective April 2026, the U.S. Army will allow new recruits between the ages of 18 and 42 years of age to enlist. The minimum age can be as young as 17 with parental permission. The previous age limit was 35 years old for the Army.The new change aligns the age limits closer with other service branches, such as the Navy (17 to 41), or the Air Force/Space Force (17 to 42), and Coast Guard (17-41). The Marine Corps has a younger limit at 17-28 years of age.Is the draft coming back?There is no active or planned draft at this time.Consideration for a draft would begin only after exhausting troops on the ground with the country's active-duty military personnel, such as full-time professional military, including National Guard and Reserves, and any volunteers or enlistees who join after the war begins.It would require congressional approval when and if and all-volunteer and professional forces are insufficient to meet the military's personnel requirements during a major national emergency.Who is required to register for Selective Service? Who would be exempt from draft?All male U.S. citizens or dual citizens residing in the United States or living abroad and male immigrants, including permanent residents, refugees, asylum seekers and undocumented, residing in the United States are legally required to register for the Selective Service if they are between 18 and 25 years of age, according to the Selective Service, excluding females and those already on active duty with the armed forces or those that are hospitalized/institutionalized.Women are not required to register for the Selective Service, nor does it accept voluntary registrations from women.Registration for the Selective Service can be done online, at the post office, via a registration form and is sometimes included in driver's license applications. While registrations are not currently automatic for men upon turning 18, federal law will change this process to full, automatic registration using government databases beginning Dec. 18, 2026, according to the Selective Service.Failing to register for the Selective Service is a federal felony punishable by up to five years in prison and fines up to $250,000, according to the Selective Service. It can also result in other penalties such as ineligibility for federal student loans, federal employment and U.S. citizenship for immigrants.Who can be drafted? Who would be drafted first?Currently, only men aged 18 through 25 who are U.S. citizens or residents (including immigrants, refugees and undocumented) would be considered for a draft.Women cannot be drafted according to the current laws. Although they can volunteer to fight in a war, they would not be considered in a draft.In the event a military draft were to get reinstated in the United States, the Selective Service would conduct a National Draft Lottery via a public, nationally televised and live-streamed lottery where a random drawing of birthdays and numbers, would be establish the order in which individuals would receive orders to report for induction into the Armed Forces.Who would be drafted in order of age, would be as follows:those whose 20th birthday falls during the year of the draft lottery21222324251918Am I registered with Selective Service? How to check registration statusTo register with the Selective Service, go to sss.gov/register/ to start registration. If you want to check your registration status, you can click here.Maria Francis is a Pennsylvania-based journalist covering trending topics across the Mid-Atlantic region.
